stem: Patrick is a six-month-old infant with severe wheeze, grunting, chest wall recession and hypoxaemia. Which one of the following is the most important next investigation to perform in this child?
explanation: This presentation is most consistent with severe bronchiolitis. In an otherwise typical case, bronchiolitis is a clinical diagnosis and routine investigations are usually unnecessary; if a test is being sought from the options, a nasopharyngeal aspirate is the most appropriate as it can help identify a viral cause, whereas blood tests, blood cultures and chest X-ray are not routine next investigations. In practice, urgent management and escalation of respiratory support are more important than investigation.

citations.title: Practice Quiz: Emergency Medicine - Breathing difficulties

rationale: The child has classic bronchiolitis features (infant, viral prodrome, wheeze/crackles, severe work of breathing, hypoxaemia). Routine investigations are generally avoided; among the listed choices, nasopharyngeal aspirate is the best fit.

optionExplanations.A: Best available option: may identify a viral pathogen and is more relevant than routine blood tests or imaging in typical bronchiolitis.
optionExplanations.B: Not usually helpful in typical bronchiolitis and does not guide immediate management.
optionExplanations.C: Not routinely indicated unless an alternative diagnosis or complication is suspected.
optionExplanations.D: May be considered if there is concern about impending respiratory failure, but it is not the most important next investigation from these options.
optionExplanations.E: Not indicated in typical viral bronchiolitis without signs of sepsis.

Instructions

The following nine questions refer to Patrick’s clinical scenario.

Clinical scenario 1 - Patrick

Patrick, a six month old infant, is brought to the emergency department with wheezing and respiratory distress. On examination he has severe chest wall retractions, grunting and is pale. His vital signs are:

RR 80/min, HR 190/min, temperature 38.0’C, SaO2 80% in room air.

The accompanying table has the normal ranges indicated in the 2010 NSW Health Standard Paediatric Observation Chart, SPOC.

Patrick has wheeze and crackles throughout his chest. There is a history of having been snuffly with a cough for the last two days. The entire family has a cold.
